others.title: C-MoA-XRT: Explainability-Aware Trust Routing for Collaborative Threat Detection in Mobile-Edge Networks
others.abstract: Threat detection in mobile-edge networks requires reliable inference from heterogeneous telemetry whose availability and evidential quality may vary over time. LLM-assisted detectors further introduce uncertainty because prediction confidence may not reflect evidence trustworthiness, while collaborative reasoning can amplify unsupported decisions. This paper proposes C-MoA-XRT, a trust-aware collaborative Mixture-of-Agents framework for resilient mobile-edge threat detection. C-MoA-XRT distributes complementary network evidence across specialized LLM agents and performs event-specific trust routing before collaborative inference. The proposed routing mechanism separates prediction confidence from decision authority by assessing the reliability, consistency, and evidential support of each specialist output. A defensive red-team reasoning stage subsequently examines the fused evidence, while an evidence-anchored decision firewall constrains unstable collaborative reasoning from overriding the calibrated detection outcome. Experiments on NF-UNSW-NB15 show that C-MoA-XRT achieves an F1 score of 0.900 with full attack recall and reduces the false-positive rate by approximately 75% relative to the evaluated single-agent RAG+LLM baseline. Under measurement drift, trust-aware evidence gating improves PR-AUC from 0.694 to 0.917 over confidence-based routing, while maintaining resilience under the evaluated telemetry-dropout and unreliable-specialist conditions. These results demonstrate that explicit control of evidence trust and reasoning authority can improve the robustness of collaborative LLM-based threat detection in mobile-edge networks.

others.title: LLM-Enabled Self-Organizing UAV Networks for Autonomous Service Provisioning
others.abstract: The growing demand for flexible and resilient low-altitude connectivity is driving UAV networks toward increasingly autonomous operation. However, existing approaches often assume known user distributions, fixed network configurations, or treat exploration, access, and backhaul separately, resulting in a gap between user discovery and end-to-end service in initially unknown environments. To address this challenge, we propose a self-organizing heterogeneous UAV networking framework, referred to as Discovery-to-Service (D2S) Network, that supports the complete process from user discovery to end-to-end service provisioning. The framework adopts a dual-timescale coordination mechanism: at the fast timescale, onboard graph reinforcement learning agents perform user exploration and local control, while at the slower timescale, a basestation-hosted LLM reconfigures the access and backhaul infrastructure based on discovered demands and the global network state. Experiments over 42 scenarios show that, compared with a heuristic connectivity-constrained grid-greedy method, the proposed framework improves effective coverage by 23.38 percentage points, terminal throughput by 55.3%, and cumulative throughput by 44.3%, demonstrating its effectiveness for autonomous network formation under unknown demand.

others.title: An Agentic AI Architecture for Zero-Touch IoT Device Onboarding and Interoperability
others.abstract: The heterogeneity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices remains a major barrier to scalable deployment, automated onboarding, and cross-platform interoperability. Device-specific protocols, software dependencies, telemetry formats, and runtime constraints often require manual configuration and ad-hoc integration logic. This paper proposes an agentic AI architecture for zero-touch IoT device onboarding, where a large language model is used as an autonomous configuration agent capable of generating device-side software, installing dependencies, validating runtime behavior, and recursively correcting failures until convergence is achieved. The proposed architecture introduces a closed-loop workflow that combines device inspection, AI-based runtime generation, remote deployment, telemetry validation, and self-correction. Interoperability is addressed through a normalized telemetry contract that abstracts device-specific behavior into a common telemetry representation. We evaluate the approach on a real IoT device by benchmarking multiple AI models under clean installation conditions in two campaigns: the original pipeline and a second pipeline assisted by a locally trained semantic context optimizer. The comparison covers convergence time, correction cycles, recursive iterations, and prompt tokens. The optimizer-assisted campaign reduced prompt redundancy and recursive recovery effort while preserving successful onboarding across all tested models. Overall, the results show that agentic AI can support zero-touch onboarding while exposing measurable differences among models in reliability, efficiency, and runtime convergence.

others.title: Ripple: Coordination-Free Message Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows at the IoT Edge
others.abstract: Distributed intelligence in IoT and edge systems increasingly runs as agentic AI: production large language model (LLM) applications execute as workflows—directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of agents and tools that exchange prompts, retrieved context, and tool outputs across end devices, edge servers, and the cloud. When many such workflows share a capacity-limited link, such as an edge gateway uplink or a regional aggregation point, that link rather than the GPU gates the communication phase, and a message that unblocks an idle agent may wait behind an unrelated bulk transfer. A dependency-aware link scheduler can mitigate this, but a scheduler that ranks messages by whole-workflow remaining work and downstream critical path requires a global, continuously updated view of every concurrent workflow, that is, a central coordinator that heterogeneous and dynamic IoT edge deployments typically lack. This paper presents Ripple, a coordination-free link scheduler in which each agent ranks only its own outgoing messages, using a local rule that prioritizes downstream criticality per unit transmission cost and applies an age credit to curb long waits. The required downstream-criticality signal is a bounded scalar initialized with the source's task descriptor, so no runtime node maintains the global graph. In an event-driven, flow-level evaluation on a shared 100 Mbps link with heavy-tailed messages (median 419 KB, 99th-percentile about 30 MB) and four DAG shapes, network waiting accounts for 46% of the mean workflow completion time (WCT) under fair sharing at offered load ρ=0.88. Ripple reduces mean and 99th-percentile WCT by 24% and 38% relative to fair sharing, and attains 9% lower mean and 27% lower tail WCT than a global-view reference heuristic while using no global state. A knowledge-horizon analysis shows that performance saturates at a one-hop view, and an ablation finds that message size and age drive most of the aggregate gain. The results use an idealized flow-level priority model; a DSCP/eBPF realization that needs no coordinator and no change to the LLM runtime is proposed but not yet evaluated.

others.title: MOSAIC: Efficient Collaborative Inference for Multi-Modal Large Language Models with Distributed Edge Computing
others.abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) enable natural language reasoning over heterogeneous sensory data, appealing to many edge AI scenarios, yet their deployment faces competing demands on latency, energy, and quality. We present MOSAIC, which adopts a component-level decomposition and distributed deployment paradigm for efficient MLLM inference at the edge, realizing three core ideas: parallel encoding, token pruning, and device-server collaboration. Specifically, for the offline stage, modality-specific encoders distilled from a unified foundation model are co-deployed with Q-Former projection on edge devices for parallel encoding, while LoRA instruction fine-tuning adapts the frozen LLM backbone to downstream tasks. For the online stage, we formulate a multi-objective optimization over latency and energy that jointly tunes token budgets, device frequencies, and quantization precision under long-term semantic accuracy constraints, achieving dynamic token pruning and device-server collaboration. We leverage Lagrangian relaxation to decompose the original problem into tractable per-slot subproblems and design an online algorithm with provable near-optimal performance and guaranteed constraint satisfaction. We implement a realistic testbed for extensive performance evaluation, which demonstrates that MOSAIC reduces latency by up to 49.8% and energy by up to 65.1% over advanced baselines while maintaining high semantic accuracy.

others.title: Model-based Zero-shot Conflict Detection Framework via Gradients in O-RAN
others.abstract: Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) enables network control through multi-vendor xApps operating both within and across layers, subnets, and domains, whose concurrent execution can trigger conflicts that are latent during the development phase. Existing conflict management approaches rely heavily on joint-execution data, which is often unavailable in practice. To address this limitation, we formalize a novel problem termed conflict reasoning, which involves identifying conflict-inducing conditions given only marginal datasets from each individual xApp. We propose ZODIAC, a three-stage framework for zero-shot conflict condition inference that comprises uncertainty-aware surrogate model training, trajectory-level diffusion training, and compositional guided denoising for efficient, physics-constrained, and reliable condition search. We derive a theoretical lower confidence bound showing that the compositional reasoning in ZODIAC serves as a principled surrogate for true conflict severity, with the epistemic penalty directly controlling the approximation gap. We evaluate ZODIAC on both the lightweight Mobile-Env platform across all three O-RAN Alliance conflict types (direct, indirect, and implicit) and a realistic NS-O-RAN-Flexric simulator. ZODIAC consistently outperforms baseline condition search methods, achieving over 20% higher True Positive Rate at Top-20, substantially stronger Spearman rank correlation, greater scenario diversity, and competitive computational efficiency. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each guidance component, with epistemic uncertainty penalties proving essential for filtering spurious conflicts. To the best of our knowledge, ZODIAC is the first framework in O-RAN that enables conflict reasoning from marginal offline data without requiring any joint-execution traces.

others.title: Demo: Multimodal Stress Monitoring with Split Federated Fine-Tuning on Mobile Devices
others.abstract: We present an end-to-end mobile system for proactive stress monitoring from wearable signals. The framework is supported by an extensible split federated learning system that enables on-device LoRA fine-tuning of large language models. By analyzing physiological data, the application distinguishes emotional states, summarizes recent trends, and provides brief, actionable suggestions. Upon detecting a negative emotional state, the paired smartwatch or smartphone proactively delivers notifications to users to encourage mindfulness. The on-site demonstration will showcase real-time sensing-inference on smartwatch-phone pairs, alongside a recorded split federated learning process that continuously learns from user private data. Our code has been open-sourced at: https://github.com/HKU-WILL-Lab/Multimodal-Stress-Monitoring-with-Split-Federated-Fine-Tuning-on-Mobile-Devices.

others.title: TrustSense: Structure-Adaptive Trust Inference for Resilient Cooperative IoT Sensing
others.abstract: Cooperative IoT sensing must assess reports from noisy, faulty, or compromised devices despite churn and changing inter-device relationships. We present TrustSense, a structure-adaptive GNN framework for per-report trust evaluation. TrustSense represents active devices as a dynamic graph and maps each report's neighborhood-based reconstruction residual to a trust score. A layer-wise soft edge mask downweights less informative dependencies, while forced anchor attention reserves a controlled share of attention for available trusted anchors. At runtime, historical consistency drives anchor-rooted credit diffusion to prioritize returning devices, and accepted reports guide subsequent evaluations. Shared GNN parameters make TrustSense inductive, enabling targeted adaptation to unseen devices without usable history. TrustSense is also location-centric, device-agnostic, and prior-free with respect to the sensing process, assuming neither a parametric sensing-value distribution nor a known propagation model. We evaluate TrustSense on synthetic RF data and real LoED traces with injected attacks. With 10% additive-bias attackers on LoED, it improves F1 by 4.25× over the strongest evaluated baseline and achieves a lower Brier score. These gains persist with up to 50% malicious devices, while inference latency remains within 230-250 ms at several thousand devices.

others.title: Poster: ProbeGuard, Budgeted Active Probing for Safe LLM Service Recomposition under Silent Semantic Drift
others.abstract: Under silent semantic drift, an upgraded edge-cloud service stays schema-compatible but changes a unit, precondition, or state transition, invalidating LLM-orchestrated compositions. ProbeGuard treats candidate behaviors as a version space and spends a small budget of safe probes to discriminate them; owner-protected executable clauses cannot be weakened by an LLM, and a service is cleared only when all evidence-compatible hypotheses agree. In 252 controlled episodes, hybrid hypothesis generation recovers 94.8% of drifted behaviors, and ProbeGuard automates 98.4% of decisions correctly while cutting harmful clearance from 5.3% to 2.7% and latency from 0.94 to 0.56 s versus the strongest deployable baseline.

others.title: Query-Aware Temporal Evidence Prefetching to Support Communication-Efficient Video AIoT Reasoning
others.abstract: Video Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) systems increasingly use vision-language models (VLMs) to answer questions about dynamic scenes, yet continuous high-resolution streaming may exceed wireless and latency budgets. We therefore study a layered setting in which the receiver always holds a low-resolution stream and requests only a limited number of high-resolution enhancement patches. Within this setting, we propose query-aware temporal semantic prefetching (QTPF), which uses the task query and prior low-resolution images to predict evidence locations in the next sampled observation before it arrives. On 14,913 LingoQA scenery questions, QTPF obtains 0.6355 Recall@5 under an OpenCLIP evidence target, compared with 0.5858 for a query-only learned model and 0.6270 for an independently trained query-aware last-frame predictor. The advantage persists under independently generated SigLIP targets, where QTPF obtains 0.5473 against 0.5328 for the last-frame predictor. With five enhancement patches, the delivered JPEG payload averages 9.77 KB, which is 20.9% below the 12.35 KB full-resolution image, and the predictor adds only 0.75 ms on an RTX 6000 Ada GPU.

others.title: Poster: When Safer AI Makes the System Less Safe: Inference Reuse and Systemic Risk in Networked Autonomy
others.abstract: Network-assisted inference can improve the decisions of autonomous agents, while reusing inference results can avoid repeated computation. However, when multiple agents reuse the same inference result, their failures become more coupled. We show that beyond a simple threshold, simultaneous failure can become more likely even though every agent is individually more accurate. We then characterize when the resource savings from reuse justify this added shared-failure risk.

others.title: MIRA: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal LLM Framework for DESH Assessment in IoT-Enabled MRI Workflows
others.abstract: Connected MRI scanners operate as networked medical devices within DICOM-based healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) workflows, but conventional connectivity primarily moves images to a Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) rather than adding task-specific reasoning near acquisition. Building on DESH-App 2.0, a preceding machine-learning contribution accepted for oral presentation at SIN Firenze 2026, this paper specifies MIRA (Multimodal Imaging Reasoning and Assessment), a vendor-neutral edge-cloud module for assessing disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid spaces (DESH). A hospital-edge gateway validates and de-identifies 3D T1-weighted DICOM studies, derives ventricular, high-convexity, and Sylvian-fissure masks with SegFormer3D, and converts each volume into a compact evidence package comprising 12 representative slices with overlays, 17 global, zonal, and ratio features, and quality-control tokens. LLaVA-Med-7B and Lingshu-7B are adapted through 4-bit QLoRA to return constrained JSON containing class, confidence, named anatomical evidence, and an abstention or quality warning. The edge-cloud partition keeps raw volumes inside the institutional network; only the compact evidence package may reach an authenticated inference service, while structured outputs return to the PACS workstation. The evaluation protocol jointly covers diagnostic discrimination, calibration, evidence agreement, unsupported claims, abstention, latency, transmitted bytes, memory demand, link-loss recovery, and multi-device interoperability. MIRA is designed to add auditable multimodal reasoning to connected MRI workflows without modifying safety-critical scanner controls.

others.title: Reliable V2X-Enabled Autonomous Driving with Explainable Federated Neuro-Symbolic Intelligence
others.abstract: Connected and autonomous vehicles rely on vehicle-to-everything (V2X) cooperation when local sensing is incomplete or delayed, as often occurs in dense traffic, occluded intersections, and roads with constrained communication. Yet many data-driven driving models remain difficult to interpret, and centralized learning requires large raw sensory data transfers that raise communication and privacy concerns. This paper proposes an explainable federated neuro-symbolic intelligence framework for reliable V2X-enabled autonomous driving. The framework combines neural perception, symbolic rule-based reasoning, fuzzy uncertainty modeling, and reliability-aware federated learning. Each vehicle trains a local decision agent from local driving and communication-context observations, while an edge or roadside unit aggregates model updates without collecting raw sensory data. The local agent also produces an interpretable rationale, including activated rules, uncertainty indicators, and risk factors associated with the selected decision. Simulation-based V2X results show that the proposed method improves decision quality, reduces missed safety-critical states, and converges faster than standard Federated Averaging (FedAvg) under vehicle-side data that are not independent and identically distributed (non-IID).

others.title: FrozenSFL: Model-Frozen Split Federated Learning for Resource-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning over Heterogeneous Edge Devices
others.abstract: Collaborative fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) at the network edge enables privacy-preserving and personalized generative intelligence, but is constrained by the limited memory and compute resources of edge devices. Traditional approaches, such as split federated learning (SFL), partition models between devices and a server, requiring iterative exchanges of activations/gradients while the server manages multiple submodels. This leads to substantial communication overhead, high activation storage costs, and severe server-side memory pressure when scaling to massive heterogeneous devices. In this paper, we propose FrozenSFL, a resource-efficient SFL framework for collaborative fine-tuning of LLMs across heterogeneous edge devices. At its core, FrozenSFL strictly freezes device-side submodels to eliminate both deviceside backpropagation and server-to-device gradient transmission, thereby removing on-device activation storage requirements and downlink communication overhead. Building upon this design, we improve the framework in two aspects. First, we design a layerwise LoRA aggregation strategy to handle structural heterogeneity introduced by device-specific model partitioning and enable efficient server-side updates. Second, we introduce a server-side feature caching mechanism that reuses invariant features, allowing subsequent training epochs to proceed offline and reducing redundant computation and communication. We implement the FrozenSFL system as an asynchronous multi-threaded pipeline, which serves as our real-world testbed for evaluation. On the device side, forward computation and data transmission are decoupled via a producer-consumer mechanism. On the server side, a first-in-first-out scheduling strategy serializes fine-tuning tasks across devices. A hybrid memory-disk streaming mechanism further buffers incoming data and ensures stable training under network variability. Extensive evaluations with representative models, including BERT-Base (0.11B), ViT-Large (0.3B), and LLaMA-2-7B (7B), validate the effectiveness of FrozenSFL. In particular, for LLaMA-2-7B, FrozenSFL can reduce device/server VRAM footprint by up to 14%/82.7% with only 1% accuracy loss, while achieving up to 6.7× fine-tuning speedup.

others.title: Demo: On-Device Agent for Personalized and Efficient Mobile Network Configuration
others.abstract: As mobile devices increasingly operate across heterogeneous access networks and diverse usage contexts, efficient network configuration requires decisions that adapt to both dynamic network conditions and individual user preferences. We demonstrate an on-device communication agent that transforms historical user network-switching behavior into personalized configuration rules. An on-device Large language model (LLM) analyzes switching records offline and generates condition-action rules capturing recurring user preferences. During real-time use, the agent retrieves matched rules locally and executes the corresponding network configuration after user confirmation, without invoking the LLM. Attendees will choose a prepared behavior trace, inspect the rule generated on the phone, and recreate its triggering context to observe an immediate network switch. The demonstration shows how separating deliberation from execution makes personalized mobile network configuration both interpretable and responsive while keeping user data and inference on the device.

others.title: Your Palm Is in My Hand: Palm-Vein Biometric Spoofing via Electromagnetic Side Channel
others.abstract: As a biometric modality, palm-vein authentication has seen growing adoption in recent years and is becoming prevalent in wallet-free payments and critical access-control applications. Although palm-vein patterns are widely regarded as nearly impossible to forge or steal, our study reveals that electromagnetic emanations induced during sensor operation can leak information correlated with a user's palm-vein characteristics, enabling attackers to reconstruct palm-vein images and spoof authentication systems. In this paper, we present PVSpy, a novel attack framework that demonstrates the feasibility of this attack. Specifically, PVSpy passively captures electromagnetic emanations radiated from palm-vein sensors, extracts features that map the captured signals to palm-vein images, and exploits diffusion models for biometric reconstructions to spoof palm-vein authentication devices. We extensively evaluate PVSpy on five commercial devices, and the recovered vein patterns exhibit a promising level of similarity. In addition, we conduct 30 end-to-end spoofing attacks against these commercial-off-the-shelf devices with different types of palm-vein sensors, and PVSpy achieves 26.7% (top-1) and 63.3% (top-3) success rates.
